I'm Manjula, Shreya's older sister. I've been helping her learn to drive our family scooter in the lane behind our building in Nashik. I can't read her mind, but here's what I saw.

I wanted to tell you something I learned this week, since you're about to start training new staff too.

I'm Binita, and in three years of college in Guwahati I've changed my major twice: from biology to economics to sociology. I've joined the photography club, the environmental group and, for one term, the dance society. Last summer I volunteered in a tea-garden school.

Ramesh called today. He asked, "So, what are you now? Still history?"
Honestly, I don't know. First year I, Divyansh, was in physics. Then I switched to history. I spent last summer cycling around Rajasthan and working at a hostel in Jodhpur. This term I joined the debating club and a theatre group.
Ramesh has already signed up for a bank job. Part of me envies how sure he sounds.
But when I cycled through those villages, I found myself asking every old man about the past. And in debating, I love the history questions. Maybe that's a clue.
I don't want to just drift, though. I'm going to write down what each thing taught me before I pick the next.
